synopsis: Robotic soft-target platforms are established in road AEB testing but are built for passenger-car speeds; Euro NCAP 2026–2028 uses ISO 19206 pedestrian and bicyclist targets, while UN R131 specifies an ISO 19206-2 child target crossing at 5 km/h [f345, f2546, f2547, f2522]. For heavy off-road validation, the recommendation is to transfer ISO 19206’s standardized-surrogate design principle rather than reuse road targets: surrogates must cover PPE-clad people, light vehicles beneath a haul truck’s nose, machines and fixed obstacles, with responses matched to each sensing modality [f2554, f2555, f2556]. Proving-ground tests provide strong complete-chain confirmation and accurate, repeatable geometry and timing references, but staged targets cannot establish statistical rates or broad coverage of weather, site objects and natural behaviour [f552, f5386, f5388, f953]. The booklet found neither an off-road ISO 19206-equivalent target standard nor publicly documented high-throughput robotic-target validation for heavy machines, and did not identify a site, chamber or target supplier handling 50–400 t machines at representative speeds; automation is therefore a candidate investment, not a proven shortcut [f15329, f566, f1166, f568]. Sensor selection should not be delayed because target realism depends on the selected sensors, and a visually convincing dummy can still have incorrect radar, lidar, ultrasonic or thermal characteristics [f570, f2912, f2913, f2914, f5389]. For a team starting from zero in October 2026, physical-test procedures, a procured or adapted soft-target kit, ground-truth specifications and independent-test-body engagement are considered realistic by mid-2027, using an ACARP Tier 1 and Tier 2 style protocol [f851].

relations.note: Both describe adapting light-vehicle procedures for heavy-vehicle stopping distances and target towing equipment.
Both report no publicly documented high-throughput robotic-target system for heavy off-road machines.

Both urge timely sensor selection because target realism depends on chosen sensors.
Both specify the same off-road surrogate classes; the glossary adds the transferable design principle.
Both require matching camera, radar, lidar and ultrasonic characteristics to each sensor.
Both warn that correct camera appearance does not ensure correct radar cross-section.
